trajectory_summary: The call opens on friction (address mismatch, a spontaneous vulnerability disclosure) and then spends nearly two-thirds of its runtime stuck in a tech-friction loop trying to get bill data from an elderly, low-tech customer. The rep eventually recovers with a verbal read-back and lands a scheduled appointment despite the customer's limited phone literacy and real-world scheduling constraints (a funeral, a daughter's shift work). The shape is mixed: real energy was lost to a slow pivot, but the rep's persistence through both the tech friction and the multi-round scheduling negotiation ultimately produced a concrete booked time.
outcome_dispute: The appointment does have a specific day and time (Monday at 7) and a channel (in-person specialist visit), so 'booked' is defensible, but it is fragile: the daughter (the co-owner/decision-maker) was never directly spoken to or confirmed, only relayed through James, and James himself asks the rep to call him to confirm attendance — 'if anything change, you call me' — which signals real uncertainty about whether the appointment holds.

observed_outcome.quote: Well, I would get you guys down for Monday at seven.
observed_outcome.reasoning: A specific day (Monday) and time (7pm) are agreed for an in-person specialist visit, meeting the 'booked' bar, but the daughter — the co-owner/decision-maker — was never directly spoken to on the call and James himself flags the plan as tentative ('if anything change, you call me'), making co_owner_confirmed false.

bill_anchor_audit.bill_quote: I just paid it today, and that was 200 and something dollars.
bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The rep acknowledges the $200+ figure with only 'Yeah. Okay. Good to know.' and moves straight into requesting the detailed kWh bill; the number is never used later as emotional leverage against the utility or tied to the value of the appointment.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep never explicitly asks 'what interested you in solar' — the call moves from intro directly into address/roof/title verify items, and the customer never volunteers a motivation (bill pain, environment, etc.) unprompted.

script_coverage.quote: Hey, James. This is Holland with Ion. I got a request you were looking into solar for your home.
I've got your address here, James, as 907 North Leamington Avenue in Chicago. Is that correct?
Is there anybody else on the title of the home with you?
Do you know how old your current roof is?
I'm assuming you're just with ComEd for your electricity.
Do you know how much you're spending on average a month with ComEd?
Just as long as you have a credit score above 670, then you'll qualify.
The only thing I need from you, James, is just a copy of your kilowatt usage on your bill.
Well, I would get you guys down for Monday at seven.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: Slow pivot on tech-friction / alternative bill-collection path
primary_coaching_focus.quote: So I'm just gonna send you a text. And then could you take a picture of that bill that you're looking at and send that over to me?
primary_coaching_focus.why: The rep burned roughly 9 minutes cycling through text-photo and email before landing on verbal readback, well past the schema's 2-minute pivot guidance; this is the single largest time-and-energy leak on the call and a repeatable, coachable behavior for future low-tech customers.

key_moments.stewart_read: The rep's intro at 00:08 references a 'request' for solar but the address the rep has on file is immediately wrong, undercutting the legitimacy the intro was meant to establish. There's no clear lead-source framing (no form reference, no Tesla framing) to anchor why this call is happening, which likely contributed to the customer's later confusion about 'what are we talking about.'

key_moments.quote: But since my wife passed, I put my daughter on my insurance.
key_moments.stewart_read: The customer discloses his wife's death directly in response to the co-owner verify question. The rep's next line is purely procedural ('Alright. Perfect. That is good to know.') with no acknowledgment of the loss before pivoting straight into the credit-score pitch.

key_moments.quote: I have no idea what my score is or nothing.
key_moments.stewart_read: When the customer can't state a credit score, the rep improvises a substitute question ('Okay. Do you, like, pay your bills on time and everything?') rather than following any defined schema path. This is exactly the ambiguity the schema's policy_question_for_kenny flags: it's unclear whether the setter should be making a stated-credit judgment call at all, and here the rep effectively waves the customer through on an unverified proxy answer.

key_moments.quote: Yeah. But hold on. Hold on. What are we talking about? Signing up for, solar stuff?
key_moments.stewart_read: The customer's confusion mid-verify about the call's purpose is handled cleanly and immediately: the rep clarifies no signup is happening and reminds him he inquired.
